edges.description: Chronic energy deficit in the highest-demand tissue, the neonatal myocardium, drives hypertrophic remodeling. The intervening steps between the bioenergetic deficit and the hypertrophic phenotype are not established for COA5.

edges.description: Accumulated circulating lactate produces the measured acidosis.
Renal excretion of the accumulated lactate load.
Elevated urinary ethylmalonic acid accompanies the metabolic decompensation. The route from the Complex IV block to ethylmalonate excretion is not established in COA5 disease.
Hepatic involvement, with abnormal liver function tests and increased hepatic echogenicity, accompanies the systemic metabolic decompensation.
The remodeling response is expressed as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

edges.description: Septal hypertrophy is a component of the hypertrophic remodeling.

edges.description: Patient fibroblasts carry the causal genotype and show the defining lesion: accumulation of an early, COX1-containing assembly intermediate with loss of the holoenzyme, reversed by wild-type COA5 re-expression.
edges.limitations: Fibroblasts are not an affected tissue in this cardiac-dominant disorder, so nothing about the cardiomyopathy can be read out here. The cells also grow poorly, which the 2025 authors identify as a practical limit on further experimentation.

edges.description: The knockout reproduces the patients' isolated Complex IV defect and resolves it further: MTCO1-containing subcomplexes accumulate, MTCO2 is absent, and the holoenzyme is lost, placing the COA5 step between MTCO1 maturation and MTCO2 incorporation.
edges.limitations: A heterologous osteosarcoma line rather than a cardiac or neural cell, and a frameshift null rather than the patients' missense allele, so it reports the consequence of complete COA5 absence rather than the consequence of p.Ala53Pro. Nothing about the cardiomyopathy or the lethal course can be observed in it.

nodes.description: Biallelic COA5 (C2orf64) variants remove a small twin-CX9C Complex IV assembly factor that acts between maturation of the mitochondrially encoded core subunit MTCO1 and the incorporation of MTCO2 into the nascent enzyme. Patient fibroblasts accumulate a small assembly intermediate containing COX1 but lacking COX2, COX4 and COX5b, and steady-state MTCO2 is selectively reduced in patient fibroblasts and skeletal muscle, so the holoenzyme is never completed. The lesion is confined to Complex IV biogenesis: the other oxidative-phosphorylation complexes are unaffected.

nodes.description: Homozygous missense variant in the twin-CX9C domain of COA5, the only pathogenic COA5 allele reported to date. Recorded in ClinVar as pathogenic for isolated cytochrome c oxidase deficiency. Its recurrence in two unrelated Turkish families raises but does not establish the possibility of a founder allele; haplotype analysis has not been performed.

Built specifically because the patient fibroblasts grow too poorly for extended biochemistry, it is the system in which complexome profiling localized the COA5-dependent step.

nodes.description: The neonatal myocardium is the tissue that fails first and hardest in COA5 deficiency. All reported patients developed cardiomyopathy; in the 2025 case it was biventricular and hypertrophic with septal hypertrophy and a non-compaction appearance of the myocardium, progressing to poor cardiac function and death. This cardiac dominance, rather than the encephalopathy that the disease name implies, is what distinguishes the COA5 phenotype within nuclear-type Complex IV deficiency.

nodes.description: Loss of assembled Complex IV blocks electron transfer from cytochrome c to molecular oxygen and the proton pumping coupled to it, collapsing oxidative ATP synthesis. In COA5 knockout cells the supercomplex containing complexes III2 and IV is lost entirely, leaving only complex I plus III2 assemblies, so the respirasome cannot form.

nodes.description: No disease-modifying therapy exists. Management is supportive: inotropic and respiratory support during cardiac and metabolic decompensation, treatment of lactic acidosis, cardiac surveillance, and anticipatory guidance. In the 2025 patient, care was explicitly directed to symptomatic management once the mitochondrial diagnosis was made, and intercurrent viral infection precipitated the fatal decompensation - so infection prevention and early escalation during intercurrent illness are the practical priorities.
